addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	import AppKit
2	import Defaults
3	
4	/// Which of the two quick switchers a keystroke opened (issue #132).
5	enum QuickSwitcherKind: Equatable {
6	  /// ⌥Tab — open workrooms, across every window.
7	  case workrooms
8	  /// ⌃Tab — the key window's current workroom's panes.
9	  case panes
10	}
11	
12	/// What the key monitor should do with a quick-switcher keystroke aimed at a particular window
13	/// (issue #132) — see `AppDelegate.switcherGate(for:in:)`, which decides it.
14	enum SwitcherGate {
15	  /// Not one of our windows: the key belongs to whatever is focused there.
16	  case passThrough
17	  /// One of ours, but with a modal up: eat the key rather than retarget a live dialog's subject.
18	  case swallow
19	  /// Go ahead on this store.
20	  case act(AppStore)
21	}
22	
23	/// The modifier a quick switcher is triggered with. Stored as a preference because a global hotkey
24	/// grabber wins over our local key monitor and there is no way to detect or beat one: AltTab,
25	/// HyperSwitch and Contexts all bind ⌥Tab by default via a CGEvent tap, which is upstream of
26	/// `NSApp.sendEvent`, so for those users the keystroke never reaches Workroom at all. Retuning the
27	/// modifier is the only possible remedy (issue #132). ⌘ combinations that the OS owns (⌘Tab, ⇧⌘Tab)
28	/// are deliberately not offered.
29	enum SwitcherModifier: String, CaseIterable, Defaults.Serializable {
30	  case option
31	  case control
32	  case commandOption
33	  case commandControl
34	
35	  var flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags {
36	    switch self {
37	    case .option: [.option]
38	    case .control: [.control]
39	    case .commandOption: [.command, .option]
40	    case .commandControl: [.command, .control]
41	    }
42	  }
43	
44	  /// Menu-style glyphs, for the keyboard-shortcuts sheet.
45	  var display: String {
46	    switch self {
47	    case .option: "⌥"
48	    case .control: "⌃"
49	    case .commandOption: "⌥⌘"
50	    case .commandControl: "⌃⌘"
51	    }
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	/// The keystroke → switcher decision, as a pure function of what an `NSEvent` contributes plus the
56	/// two configured modifiers (issue #132).
57	///
58	/// Deliberately **not** added to `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut`. That list is a static allowlist,
59	/// and whether Tab belongs to the app depends on runtime state — a workroom with one pane has nothing
60	/// to switch to, so ⌃Tab must reach the TUI. The codebase already resolved this same fork the same
61	/// way: ⌃⌘arrows is deliberately unreserved so it passes through at a split's edge. The `AppDelegate`
62	/// monitor runs inside `NSApp.sendEvent` *before* key-equivalent dispatch, so when the switcher does
63	/// act the surface never sees the key regardless.
64	enum QuickSwitcherKey {
65	  /// Tab. Matched by keyCode, not characters, so it is layout-stable (and ⇧Tab still reads as Tab).
66	  static let tabKeyCode: UInt16 = 48
67	
68	  /// The switcher this keystroke triggers, and whether ⇧ makes it step backwards. `nil` for anything
69	  /// that isn't Tab with exactly one configured trigger modifier (⇧ aside).
70	  nonisolated static func classify(
71	    keyCode: UInt16, flags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags,
72	    workroomModifier: SwitcherModifier = Defaults[.switcherWorkroomModifier],
73	    paneModifier: SwitcherModifier = Defaults[.switcherPaneModifier]
74	  ) -> (kind: QuickSwitcherKind, reverse: Bool)? {
75	    guard keyCode == tabKeyCode else { return nil }
76	    let relevant = flags.intersection([.command, .shift, .option, .control])
77	    let reverse = relevant.contains(.shift)
78	    let base = relevant.subtracting(.shift)
79	    guard !base.isEmpty else { return nil }  // bare Tab belongs to the terminal (shell completion)
80	    // Workrooms win a tie, so a user who sets both modifiers the same still gets a working ⌥Tab
81	    // rather than an unreachable pane switcher.
82	    if base == workroomModifier.flags { return (.workrooms, reverse) }
83	    if base == paneModifier.flags { return (.panes, reverse) }
84	    return nil
85	  }
86	}
87	
88	/// The quick switcher itself (issue #132), stage 1: every press commits immediately, ordered by
89	/// most-recent use rather than position.
90	///
91	/// ```
92	///   ⌥Tab      items (MRU):  [ current  prev  older … ]  → commit items[1]
93	///   ⇧⌥Tab                                               → commit items[count - 1]
94	/// ```
95	///
96	/// Stage 2 adds the held-modifier rail on top of the same item collection, and moves the commit to
97	/// modifier release.
98	@MainActor
99	enum QuickSwitcher {
100	  /// Act on a switcher keystroke. Returns whether it actually switched — the key monitor consumes the
101	  /// event only then, so ⌃Tab still reaches a TUI in a workroom that has nothing to switch to.
102	  @discardableResult
103	  static func step(
104	    _ kind: QuickSwitcherKind, reverse: Bool, in store: AppStore,
105	    registry: WindowRegistry = .shared, recency: SwitcherRecency = .shared
106	  ) -> Bool {
107	    switch kind {
108	    case .workrooms:
109	      stepWorkrooms(reverse: reverse, in: store, registry: registry, recency: recency)
110	    case .panes: stepPanes(reverse: reverse, in: store, recency: recency)
111	    }
112	  }
113	
114	  // MARK: Workrooms (⌥Tab, every window)
115	
116	  /// Every window's open workrooms, MRU-ordered. Windows with a sheet/dialog up are excluded: raising
117	  /// one and moving its selection would leave its own modal describing a workroom the app is no longer
118	  /// pointed at — for the commit sheet, that is a wrong-target VCS write.
119	  static func workroomSlots(
120	    registry: WindowRegistry = .shared, recency: SwitcherRecency = .shared
121	  ) -> [WorkroomSlot] {
122	    let slots = registry.allStores
123	      .filter { !$0.hasModalPresentation }
124	      .flatMap { store in
125	        store.displayedWorkroomTargets().map {
126	          WorkroomSlot(store: store, sid: $0.sid, target: $0.target)
127	        }
128	      }
129	    return recency.workroomOrder(slots)
130	  }
131	
132	  private static func stepWorkrooms(
133	    reverse: Bool, in store: AppStore, registry: WindowRegistry, recency: SwitcherRecency
134	  ) -> Bool {
135	    let slots = workroomSlots(registry: registry, recency: recency)
136	    guard slots.count > 1 else { return false }
137	    let current = store.selectedTargetID.flatMap { sid in
138	      slots.firstIndex { $0.store === store && $0.sid == sid }
139	    }
140	    let next = destination(from: current, count: slots.count, reverse: reverse)
141	    return commit(slots[next], from: store)
142	  }
143	
144	  /// Switch to one workroom slot. Shared by the tap-only path above and the held-modifier session's
145	  /// release commit (T10), so the two can't diverge on the raise-then-select ordering.
146	  @discardableResult
147	  static func commit(_ slot: WorkroomSlot, from store: AppStore) -> Bool {
148	    guard let target = slot.store, target !== store || slot.sid != store.selectedTargetID else {
149	      return false  // already here: no raise, no selection write, no history entry
150	    }
151	    if !NSApp.isActive { NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true) }
152	    // Raise first, then select: `AppStore.persistsSidebarPrefs` keys on being `lastActiveStore`, so
153	    // the registry's didBecomeKey observer must have run before the selection write.
154	    target.hostWindow?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
155	    target.openExisting(slot.sid)
156	    return true
157	  }
158	
159	  // MARK: Panes (⌃Tab, the current workroom)
160	
161	  /// The selected workroom's panes in MRU order, or `[]` when nothing is selected.
162	  static func paneTabs(in store: AppStore, recency: SwitcherRecency = .shared) -> [TerminalTab] {
163	    guard let target = store.selectedTarget, !target.isMissing else { return [] }
164	    return recency.paneOrder(store.terminals.tabs(for: target))
165	  }
166	
167	  private static func stepPanes(
168	    reverse: Bool, in store: AppStore, recency: SwitcherRecency
169	  ) -> Bool {
170	    guard let target = store.selectedTarget, !target.isMissing else { return false }
171	    let tabs = paneTabs(in: store, recency: recency)
172	    guard tabs.count > 1 else { return false }
173	    let activeID = store.terminals.activeTab(for: target)?.id
174	    let current = activeID.flatMap { id in tabs.firstIndex { $0.id == id } }
175	    let next = destination(from: current, count: tabs.count, reverse: reverse)
176	    return commit(pane: tabs[next].id, in: store)
177	  }
178	
179	  /// Switch to one pane by id. Shared with the held-modifier session's release commit (T10).
180	  @discardableResult
181	  static func commit(pane id: TerminalTab.ID, in store: AppStore) -> Bool {
182	    guard let target = store.selectedTarget, !target.isMissing else { return false }
183	    guard store.terminals.activeTab(for: target)?.id != id else { return false }
184	    guard store.terminals.tabs(for: target).contains(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return false }
185	    // `select`, not `focus`: it also promotes the owning workroom in a split and takes keyboard focus.
186	    store.terminals.select(id, for: target)
187	    return true
188	  }
189	
190	  // MARK: Stepping
191	
192	  /// The item a single press lands on. From the head of an MRU list, forward is "the one before this"
193	  /// and backward is the least-recently-used — so a tap flips to where you just were, and tapping
194	  /// again flips back (the commit re-orders MRU). When the current place isn't in the list at all (a
195	  /// root with no terminals, a window with a modal), enter at the most recent / least recent end.
196	  nonisolated static func destination(from current: Int?, count: Int, reverse: Bool) -> Int {
197	    guard let current else { return reverse ? count - 1 : 0 }
198	    return AppStore.wrapped(index: current, by: reverse ? -1 : 1, count: count)
199	  }
200	}

After reading the diff and the surrounding `QuickSwitcher.swift` / `WorkroomApp.swift` context, this change is purely a UI/keyboard-shortcut controller for a macOS Tab-switcher session:

- No new HTTP/RPC/IPC entry points that receive attacker-controlled data. The sole "input" is `NSEvent` from the OS user-input pipeline and `NSEvent.modifierFlags` / `NSEvent.mouseLocation` snapshots.
- No new shell/exec/SQL/eval/filesystem/URL/HTML/deserialization/template sinks are added. The only "sinks" reached are `NSApp.activate`, `makeKeyAndOrderFront`, `store.terminals.select`, `target.openExisting`, and `NSAccessibility.post` (announcement text is a workroom label or tab title — user-owned local strings, not a PII/observability sink).
- `Defaults[.switcherWorkroomModifier]` / `Defaults[.switcherPaneModifier]` are `enum SwitcherModifier` values with a fixed `.flags` mapping — no injection surface, no allowlist‑style semantic escape.
- Sibling‑path gate parity: the `hasModalPresentation` gate previously enforced at `workroomSlots` collection time is now covered by `isAlive` inside `reconcileItems`. That is a UX/correctness concern (a modal presented mid‑gesture is only pruned on `willCloseNotification`, not on modal open), not a security boundary crossing — a switch to a window that has raised a sheet still cannot bypass any authorization or write to any external system.
- Timers on `.common` run-loop mode, weak-self capture in observers, and monitor placement ordering are all defensive UI concerns, not security controls.
- Parser/validator differentials, IaC omissions, CI/CD trust, over-broad grants, stale identity mappings, fail-open state drift, security-registry fanout, gate/action field mismatch, resource-bound placement, under-validated sink args: none apply — no such surfaces are touched.

No security-relevant defect identified.
